newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Joint stock banks set to merge in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Joint stock banks set to merge in Vietnam.

text.p: Two of Vietnam's 53 commercial joint stock banks plan a merger to bolster their capital base and compete in the country's fast-growing financial services market, a senior executive at one of the banks said on Friday.
The executive of Dong Thap Bank, who declined to be named, said plans for a merger with Ho Chi Minh City's Phuong Nam Bank were expected to be formally approved by the central bank next month.
The new bank's balance sheet assets would be roughly 300 billion dong ($26.9 million).
The Tuoi Tre journal said two other joint stock banks from the south of the country, Vien Dong and Nam Do, would join forces to create a bank with capital of 200 billion dong ($17.9 million).

Vietnam, which began reforming its economy along market lines in the late 1980s, created four big state-run commercial banks out of the central bank in 1990. A host of smaller joint stock banks, which are owned by private shareholders, sprang up after that.
However, the state-owned banks still account for the lion's share of deposits and loans and some of the joint stock banks are believed to have dangerously high levels of overdue loans.
Unlike the state banks, they cannot count on the government to bail them out when trouble looms.

State Bank of Vietnam Deputy Governor Do Que Luong said last month that the central bank would take steps to ensure adequate supervision of the joint-stock banks and said several of them could merge to ensure an adequate capital base.

The Dong Thap and Phuong Nam banks are likely to be the first to join forces. However, foreign bankers said new regulations imposing minimum capital levels were likely to trigger more mergers or the offer of shares to foreign investors.
Three banks have already sold shares to foreign investors to raise capital, including the Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Private Enterprises, Maritime Bank and Asian Commercial Bank.
According to a recent World Bank report, Vietnam's finance, banking and insurance sector has grown by more than 20 percent a year since 1994.
